title: Linked List Cycle
statement_short: Given head, the head of a linked list, determine if the linked list has a cycle in it. A cycle exists if there is some node in the list that can be reached again by continuously following the next pointer.
hint: Node count up to 10^4 dictates an O(n) time solution, while O(1) space requires fast and slow pointer traversal.
keywords: node in the list that can be reached again
why_not: Right: Linked List (Fast & Slow) applies Floyd's Cycle-Finding Algorithm to detect pointer collision in O(n) time and O(1) space. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Storing node references in a set detects cycles in O(n) time, but consumes O(n) auxiliary memory. Not Two Pointers: General two-pointer array techniques assume indexed contiguous access, whereas fast & slow pointers specifically handle linked list node links. Not Graph BFS: Queue-based graph traversal tracks visited nodes using extra O(n) memory instead of in-place pointer movement.
